0|a904a0693c189691eeee64f6c6b188bd7dc244e9|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"inet: stop leaking jiffies on the wire
Historically linux tried to stick to RFC 791
for IPv4 ID field generation.
RFC 6864 made clear that no matter how hard we try
we can not ensure unicity of IP ID within maximum
lifetime for all datagrams with a given source
address/destination address/protocol tuple.
Linux uses a per socket inet generator (inet_id)
at connection startup with a XOR of 'jiffies' and other
fields that appear clear on the wire.
Thiemo Nagel pointed that this strategy is a privacy
concern as this provides 16 bits of entropy to fingerprint
devices.
Let's switch to a random starting point
good as far as RFC 6864 is concerned and does not leak
anything critical.
